what_helped: Simple event-first query ('attack Oman oil facilities 2026') immediately surfaced a Wikipedia article with dedicated title '2026 Iranian strikes on Oman' — the title alone is dispositive
JPost article directly covering this tweet's false flag claim appeared in first-round results without needing a targeted query
The IRGC's contradictory self-incrimination (claiming responsibility while Iranian officials denied involvement) is the strongest counter-evidence and appeared in round-2 results
Searching for the weapon type ('Shahed') confirmed attribution via physical evidence angle
what_hurt: Nothing significantly hurt — this event is exceptionally well-documented with near-unanimous source attribution to Iran
Iran's denial strategy (IRGC claims responsibility, Foreign Ministry denies) creates surface-level ambiguity that a naive one-shot LLM might treat as genuine uncertainty
insights.would_multipass_help: no — the first two queries immediately returned Wikipedia, Bloomberg, Al Jazeera, CNN, and a JPost article directly about the false flag claim. All the meaningful evidence was in round 1.
insights.deepseek_advice: For official-account denial tweets during active conflicts, always search the event name + year first (e.g., '2026 Iranian strikes on Oman') — Wikipedia often has a dedicated article that resolves attribution definitively. Then search for the specific denial ('Iran embassy false flag Oman') to find fact-check coverage of the exact claim. Look for contradictions within the denying party's own statements (IRGC claiming responsibility while the Foreign Ministry denies).
